Before foreign travelling had become either quite so easy or quite so fashionable as it is now, the part of France most commonly explored by English tourists was Normandy. Antiquarian inquirers, in particular, hardly went anywhere else, and we suspect that with many of them a tour in France, as Mr.

39905-upsidonia.title: Upsidonia
39905-upsidonia.creator: Archibald Marshall
39905-upsidonia.description: A book by Archibald Marshall. ways been the entrance to regions of mystery, in which anything may happen. So I immediately accepted the invitation to visit these caves, which were only a few hundred yards away from the main road.

8725-the-three-cities-trilogy-rome-volum.title: Rome
8725-the-three-cities-trilogy-rome-volum.creator: Unknown
8725-the-three-cities-trilogy-rome-volum.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. a murky sea, but by degrees his eyes grew accustomed to the dimness. The vast expanse was only lighted by the four candelabra at the corners of the obelisk and by infrequent lamps skirting the buildings which run on either hand towards the Basilica.

arxiv-2111-14122.title: Cross-Task Consistency Learning Framework for Multi-Task Learning
arxiv-2111-14122.creator: Akihiro Nakano, Shi Chen, and Kazuyuki Demachi
arxiv-2111-14122.description: Abstract Multi-task learning (MTL) is an active field in deep learning in which we train a model to jointly learn multiple tasks by exploiting relationships between the tasks. It has been shown that MTL helps the model share the learned features between tasks and enhance predictions compared to when learning each task independently.

arxiv-2211-08674.title: Multiphoton Correlations between Quantum Images
arxiv-2211-08674.creator: Serge Massar, Fabrice Devaux, Eric Lantz
arxiv-2211-08674.description: Abstract Experimental demonstrations of entangled quantum images produced through parametric downconversion have so far been confined to studying two photon correlations. Here we show that multiphoton correlations between quantum images are accessible experimentally and exhibit many new features including being sensitive to the phase of the bi-photon wavefunction.

arxiv-2211-16109.title: Higher Chow cycles on a family of Kummer surfaces
arxiv-2211-16109.creator: Ken Sato
arxiv-2211-16109.description: Abstract . We construct a collection of families of higher Chow cycles of type ( 2 , 1 ) (2,1) on a 2-dimensional family of Kummer surfaces, and prove that for a very general member, they generate a subgroup of rank ≥ 18 \geq 18 in the indecomposable part of the higher Chow group.

arxiv-2302-08712.title: quantile-LSTM: A Robust LSTM for Anomaly Detection in Time Series Data
arxiv-2302-08712.creator: Snehanshu Saha, Jyotirmoy Sarkar, Soma Dhavala, Santonu Sarkar, Preyank Mota
arxiv-2302-08712.description: Abstract Anomalies refer to the departure of systems and devices from their normal behaviour in standard operating conditions. An anomaly in an industrial device can indicate an upcoming failure, often in the temporal direction. In this paper, we make two contributions: 1) we estimate conditional quantiles and consider three different ways to define anomalies based on the estimated quantiles.

arxiv-2304-04862.title: A few-shot graph Laplacian-based approach for improving the accuracy of low-fidelity data
arxiv-2304-04862.creator: Orazio Pinti, Assad A. Oberai
arxiv-2304-04862.description: Abstract Low-fidelity data is typically inexpensive to generate but inaccurate. On the other hand, high-fidelity data is accurate but expensive to obtain. Multi-fidelity methods use a small set of high-fidelity data to enhance the accuracy of a large set of low-fidelity data.

arxiv-2403-06936.title: Counterfactual Reasoning with Knowledge Graph Embeddings
arxiv-2403-06936.creator: Lena Zellinger, Andreas Stephan, Benjamin Roth
arxiv-2403-06936.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Lena Zellinger, Andreas Stephan, Benjamin Roth. Knowledge graph embeddings (KGEs) were originally developed to infer true but missing facts in incomplete knowledge repositories. In this paper, we link knowledge graph completion and counterfactual reasoning via our new task CFKGR. We model the original world state as a knowledge graph, hypothetical scenarios as edges added to the graph, and plausible changes to the graph as inferences from logical rules.

arxiv-2411-15519.title: Risk Management with Feature-Enriched Generative Adversarial Networks (FE-GAN)
arxiv-2411-15519.creator: Ling Chen
arxiv-2411-15519.description: Abstract Abstract This paper investigates the application of Feature-Enriched Generative Adversarial Networks (FE-GAN) in financial risk management, with a focus on improving the estimation of Value at Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES). FE-GAN enhances existing GANs architectures by incorporating an additional input sequence derived from preceding data to improve model performance.

arxiv-2506-03719.title: On the Closed-Form of Flow Matching: Generalization Does Not Arise from Target Stochasticity
arxiv-2506-03719.creator: Quentin Bertrand, Anne Gagneux, Mathurin Massias, Rémi Emonet
arxiv-2506-03719.description: Abstract Modern deep generative models can now produce high-quality synthetic samples that are often indistinguishable from real training data. A growing body of research aims to understand why recent methods – such as diffusion and flow matching techniques – generalize so effectively.

arxiv-2506-08686.title: Brevity is the soul of sustainability: Characterizing LLM response lengths
arxiv-2506-08686.creator: Soham Poddar*, Paramita Koley*, Janardan Misra, Sanjay Podder, Navveen Balani, Niloy Ganguly, Saptarshi Ghosh
arxiv-2506-08686.description: Abstract A significant portion of the energy consumed by Large Language Models (LLMs) arises from their inference processes; hence developing energy-efficient methods for inference is crucial. While several techniques exist for inference optimization, output compression remains relatively unexplored, with only a few preliminary efforts addressing this aspect.

arxiv-2507-06111.title: Safe Domain Randomization via Uncertainty-Aware Out-of-Distribution Detection and Policy Adaptation
arxiv-2507-06111.creator: Mohamad H. Danesh, Maxime Wabartha, Stanley Wu, Joelle Pineau, Hsiu-Chin Lin
arxiv-2507-06111.description: Abstract Deploying reinforcement learning (RL) policies in real-world involves significant challenges, including distribution shifts, safety concerns, and the impracticality of direct interactions during policy refinement. Existing methods, such as domain randomization (DR) and off-dynamics RL, enhance policy robustness by direct interaction with the target domain, an inherently unsafe practice.

arxiv-2507-07619.title: Towards conservative inference in credal networks using belief functions: the case of credal chains
arxiv-2507-07619.creator: Marco Sangalli, Thomas Krak, Cassio De Campos
arxiv-2507-07619.description: Abstract This paper explores belief inference in credal networks using Dempster-Shafer theory. By building on previous work, we propose a novel framework for propagating uncertainty through a subclass of credal networks, namely chains. The proposed approach efficiently yields conservative intervals through belief and plausibility functions, combining computational speed with robust uncertainty representation.

arxiv-2511-06402.title: SugarTextNet: A Transformer-Based Framework for Detecting Sugar Dating-Related Content on Social Media with Context-Aware Focal Loss
arxiv-2511-06402.creator: Lionel Z. WangThe Hong Kong Polytechnic University zhe-leo.wang@connect.polyu.hk, Yulu HuangThe University of Hong Kong u3631383@connect.hku.hk, Shihan BenThe University of Hong Kong u3641005@connect.hku.hk, Simeng QinNortheastern University qinsimeng@neuq.edu.cn
arxiv-2511-06402.description: Abstract Sugar dating-related content has rapidly proliferated on mainstream social media platforms, giving rise to serious societal and regulatory concerns, including commercialization of intimate relationships and the normalization of transactional relationships. Detecting such content is highly challenging due to the prevalence of subtle euphemisms, ambiguous linguistic cues, and extreme class imbalance in real-world data.

arxiv-2512-10190.title: Andrásfai–Erdős–Sós theorem under max-degree constraints
arxiv-2512-10190.creator: Xizhi Liu, Sijie Ren, Jian Wang
arxiv-2512-10190.description: Abstract We establish the following strengthening of the celebrated Andrásfai–Erdős–Sós theorem: If G G is an n n -vertex K r + 1 K_{r+1} -free graph whose minimum degree δ ⁡ ( G ) \delta(G) and maximum degree Δ ⁡ ( G ) \Delta(G) satisfy δ ⁡ ( G ) > min ⁡ { 3 ​ r − 4 3

arxiv-2601-21481.title: Compressed Sensing-Driven Near-Field Localization Exploiting Array of Subarrays
arxiv-2601-21481.creator: Sai Pavan Deram 1 2 , Jacopo Pegoraro 4 , Javier Lorca Hernando 3 , Jesus O. Lacruz 2 , Joerg Widmer 2
arxiv-2601-21481.description: Abstract Near-field localization for ISAC requires large-aperture arrays, making fully-digital implementations prohibitively complex and costly. While sparse subarray architectures can reduce cost, they introduce severe estimation ambiguity from grating lobes. To address both issues, we propose SHARE (Sparse Hierarchical Angle-Range Estimation), a novel two-stage sparse recovery algorithm. SHARE operates in two stages.

plos-pone-0011786.title: KRIT1 Regulates the Homeostasis of Intracellular Reactive Oxygen Species
plos-pone-0011786.creator: Luca Goitre, Fiorella Balzac, Simona Degani et al.
plos-pone-0011786.description: PLOS ONE research article. KRIT1 is a gene responsible for Cerebral Cavernous Malformations (CCM), a major cerebrovascular disease characterized by abnormally enlarged and leaky capillaries that predispose to seizures, focal neurological deficits, and fatal intracerebral hemorrhage. Comprehensive analysis

pmc-10608153.title: Paradigm Shift: Candida parapsilosis sensu stricto as the Most Prevalent Candida Species Isolated from Bloodstream Infections with Increasing Azole-Non-Susceptibility Rates: Trends from 2015–2022 Survey
pmc-10608153.creator: Iacopo Franconi, Cosmeri Rizzato, Arianna Tavanti, Marco Falcone, Antonella Lupetti, Michael A Pfaller
pmc-10608153.description: Candidemia is the fourth most common healthcare-related bloodstream infection. In recent years, incidence rates of Candida parapsilosis have been on the rise, with differences in prevalence and antifungal susceptibility between countries. The aim of the present study was to evaluate temporal changes in prevalence and antifungal susceptibility of C. parapsilosis among other species causing candidemia.

pmc-10650570.title: Toward Structural Health Monitoring with the MyShake Smartphone Network
pmc-10650570.creator: Sarina C. Patel, Selim Günay, Savvas Marcou, Yuancong Gou, Utpal Kumar, Richard M. Allen
pmc-10650570.description: The field of structural health monitoring (SHM) faces a fundamental challenge related to accessibility. While analytical and empirical models and laboratory tests can provide engineers with an estimate of a structure’s expected behavior under various loads, measurements of actual buildings require the installation and maintenance of sensors to collect observations. This is costly in terms of power and resources.

pmc-11503273.title: Protein Extraction Methods Suitable for Muscle Tissue Proteomic Analysis
pmc-11503273.creator: Lorenza Vantaggiato, Claudia Landi, Enxhi Shaba, Daniela Rossi, Vincenzo Sorrentino, Luca Bini, Jianxin Sun
pmc-11503273.description: Muscle tissue is one of the most dynamic and plastic tissues of the mammalian body and covers different roles, such as force generation and metabolic control. Muscular proteomics provides an important opportunity to reveal the molecular mechanisms behind muscle pathophysiology. To ensure successful proteomic analysis, it is necessary to have an efficient and reproducible protein extraction method.

pmc-11558206.title: In situ‐crosslinked Zippersomes enhance cardiac repair by increasing accumulation and retention
pmc-11558206.creator: Natalie E Jasiewicz, Kuo‐Ching Mei, Hannah M Oh, Emily E Bonacquisti, Ameya Chaudhari, Camryn Byrum, Brian C Jensen, Juliane Nguyen
pmc-11558206.description: Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)‐derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) are a promising treatment for myocardial infarction (MI), but their therapeutic efficacy is limited by inefficient accumulation at the target site. A minimally invasive MSC EV therapy that enhances EV accumulation at the disease site and extends EV retention could significantly improve post‐infarct cardiac regeneration.

pmc-11605366.title: S. cerevisiae ERG5DeltaNTH1DeltaAMS1Delta construction enhancing stress tolerance for ethanol production increase in the presence of inhibitors and mechanism analysis based on the comparative transcriptomics
pmc-11605366.creator: Peizhou Yang, Zhuanzhuan Lin, Jianchao Chen, Shuying Jiang, Zhi Zheng, Kanglin Wang
pmc-11605366.description: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is considered the most promising large-scale production strain with ethanol as the main product. The fermentation of Saccharomyces cerevisiae is generally inhibited under various stress conditions. Various inhibitors in the hydrolysate severely inhibit yeast proliferation and yeast accumulation. In this study, S.

pmc-11690940.title: ACCEPTABILITY AND PRELIMINARY EFFICACY OF BE EPIC-VR TRAINING ON FRONTLINE HEALTH CARE WORKERS
pmc-11690940.creator: Marie Savundranayagam, Grace Norris, Annette Schumann, Anya Sarma, Jennifer Campos, Joseph Orange
pmc-11690940.description: Be EPIC-VR is a person-centered communication (PCC) training program designed for healthcare providers working in dementia care. It is the first virtual reality (VR) program to use conversational artificial intelligence to train users to communicate with avatars depicting persons living with dementia (PLWD). The current study examined the acceptability and preliminary efficacy of Be EPIC-VR training.

pmc-12437609.title: Supramodal and modality-specific neural information supports multi-feature prediction errors across cortical levels
pmc-12437609.creator: Maria Niedernhuber, Francesca Fardo, Micah Allen, Tristan Bekinschtein
pmc-12437609.description: Predictive coding posits that the brain actively anticipates inputs from different senses, generating prediction errors when incoming information deviates from internal expectations. While much research has focused on prediction errors elicited by violations of single sensory features, natural environments frequently present more complex events deviating across multiple stimulus dimensions and sensory modalities.

pmc-12577093.title: An integrative analysis of transcriptome, methylome and single-cell RNA sequencing data identifies UBE2H as a marker of oxaliplatin resistance in colorectal cancer
pmc-12577093.creator: Jinman Fang, Qizhi Zhu, Bo Hong, Xueling Li, Hongzhi Wang
pmc-12577093.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Metastatic colorectal cancer is commonly treated with oxaliplatin. However, patients may develop resistance to treatment over time, and currently, there are no validated predictive biomarkers for this resistance. A differential analysis of the transcriptome and DNA methylome of colorectal cancer cell lines, classified by their varying IC50 values for oxaliplatin, revealed that genes associated with resistance were enriched for interferon regulatory factor pathways.

pmc-12646092.title: Primary healthcare providers’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding cancer screening recommendation and referral in Georgia, 2023
pmc-12646092.creator: Marina Topuridze, Ana Kareli, Givi Javashvili, Nino Kiknadze, Nino Shiukashvili, Teona Todua, Tamar Melikidze, Ketevan Khetsuriani, Davit Otiashvili
pmc-12646092.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionCancer screening uptake in Georgia is only 13%. pmc-12649505.title: Respiratory Bacteria and Antimicrobial Resistance Genes Detected by Long-Read Metagenomic Sequencing Following Feedlot Arrival, Subsequent Treatment Risk and Phenotypic Resistance in Feedlot Calves
pmc-12649505.creator: Jennifer N. Abi Younes, Lianne McLeod, Stacey R. Lacoste, Zhijian Chai, Emily K. Herman, E. Luke McCarthy, John R. Campbell, Sheryl P. Gow, Paul Stothard, Matthew G. Links, Simon J. G. Otto, Cheryl L. Waldner
pmc-12649505.description: Background/Objectives: Long-read metagenomic sequencing can assign antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) to speciated bacterial reads. This study evaluated whether metagenomic data from respiratory bacteria derived from feedlot calves sampled in the early feeding period were associated with subsequent bovine respiratory disease (BRD) treatment and phenotypic antimicrobial resistance (AMR) at treatment.

pmc-12705700.title: Evaluating multi-source precipitation data for streamflow simulation using the SWAT model in the Alpine Manas River Basin, Northwest China
pmc-12705700.creator: Li Tan, Chanjuan Zan, Tie Liu, Jiayu Xiong, Aoxiang Zhang
pmc-12705700.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Due to the influence of topography, climate, and other factors, the applicability of precipitation products varies significantly across different regions. Investigating the differences among multi-source precipitation products and their suitability for streamflow simulation in cold and alpine basins not only helps to reveal the advantages and limitations of each product but also plays an important role in improving the accuracy and application of hydrological models.

pmc-13061593.title: Hepatitis B knowledge, attitudes and practices among health-care workers in Vanuatu, 2024
pmc-13061593.creator: Leila Bell, Kaylene Kalmos, Annie Taissets, Florita Toa, Sereana Natuman, Mark Stoové, Margaret Hellard, Nicole Allard, Caroline van Gemert
pmc-13061593.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThe prevalence of chronic hepatitis B in Vanuatu is high, at approximately 9%. While immunization has been available for infants since 1989, subsets of the adult population remain susceptible, including health-care workers.

pmc-13217433.title: Assessing the Alignment of Long-Term Care Insurance Benefits and Service Provision: Evidence from Shandong, China and Implications for Implementation Risk
pmc-13217433.creator: Zhiyan Han, Xinping Wang, Huifen Ma, Haiyan Qu
pmc-13217433.description: PurposeThis study assesses the alignment between Long-Term Care Insurance (LTCI) benefit levels and service supply across 16 prefecture-level cities in Shandong Province, China. This study aims to identify whether mismatches exist between LTCI benefits and long-term care service supply across cities in Shandong Province.

pmc-13277747.title: Artificial Sweeteners and Autoimmune Diseases: Insights From Integrative Bioinformatics and Mendelian Randomization
pmc-13277747.creator: Yupei Liu, Jizhen Huang, Xue Hu, Shan Tian, Jiao Li, Shiyun Tan, Weiguo Dong

pmc-13540616.title: Neural Evidence for Action-Related Somatosensory Predictions
pmc-13540616.creator: Caoimhe Moran, Hinze Hogendoorn, Ayelet N. Landau
pmc-13540616.description: The tactile consequences of self-initiated movements are thought to be predicted by a forward model (FM), yet the precise neural implementation of these predictions remains unclear. In nonmotor contexts, expectations are thought to activate sensory neurons tuned toward the expected stimulus. This acts as a predictive template against which afferent sensory input is compared.

pmc-13610252.title: Perceived Noise Levels in Intensive Care Units and Their Self-Reported Adverse Effects on Nurses in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13610252.creator: Nabat Almalki, Atheer Asiri, Lama Alkhaldi, Huda Majrashi, Abeer Almotairi, Amal Alfifi, Hind Althobaiti, Badriah Althubaiti, Jawharah Alhufayyan, Bushra Alshammari, Mawahib Almalki
pmc-13610252.description: Background/Objectives: Intensive care units (ICUs) are acoustically demanding environments in which nurses are continuously exposed to alarms, medical equipment, and staff activity. This study assessed ICU nurses’ perceived internal and external noise levels and their perceived noise-related adverse effects, and examined whether these perceptions differed according to demographic and work-related characteristics.
